# 1.2.60 - the GM's browser decides

The fourth stage on the way to 1.3.0, and the second security one. Most of
what happens in this game is written by the GM's browser at a player's
request. Until now the GM's browser took many of those requests at their word.
It now checks each one against who really sent it and what the world says,
and refuses the rest. Nothing here asks a world to be migrated.

## Changed

- **Every request a player's browser sends to yours is judged there**: who
  sent it, whether that player plays the character or may see the project,
  and whether the room, the stage of an incident and the turn allow it. This
  covers projects and sabotage, Observe, the clean-up after a murder, Analyze,
  crisis actions, Hope and Despair Calls, traces, search tokens, traps, fog
  and sending a token back after a refused move.
- **Daggerheart's own requests are checked the same way.** Some Daggerheart
  features ask the GM's browser to make a change for a player. The ones
  Daggerheart's features send for a player still work; anything else is
  refused. A few features this game keeps to the GM stop with a refusal:
  placing an area, starting a new countdown, and healing or harming another
  student with an ability. Do those for the player.
- **Taking something back needs a Reroll just before.** A Reroll undoes the
  first result before it replays the action; the GM's browser now accepts that
  undo only right after the same player rerolled a roll of the same
  character, once for each kind of thing taken back.
- **A refused request changes nothing, and everybody knows.** The player is
  told the GM's client refused it, the refusal is in the Debug log with their
  name, and a Daggerheart change the game does not expect puts a card in the
  GM's chat. A request that was waited on - a sabotage, a Support Call - stops
  waiting straight away.
- **A character shared as Owner with every player is put back to Observer**,
  including from the Configure Ownership window, and the GMs are told.
- **A player's edit of what their Truth Bullet says or is, is put back**, and
  never carried to the other copies of the same trace.
- **Fear is never refused.** If a player's rolls move it more often than you
  saw them roll, you get a note.
- **The Despair bar shows a pool's name even when it is the only pool.** A
  lone pool used to read just "Despair", so a table that went from two GMs to
  one lost the Monokuma's name from the bar. It now shows the name set in
  Despair Flow, or the account's name when none is set.
- With the setting that stops players editing their own sheet turned off,
  players can click Hope and the traits again; the sheet used to swallow the
  click whatever the setting said.

## Checked

- The headless suite and the eleven scenarios. New in the suite: R132-R149.
  New in the security scenario: a request a player's own browser never sends,
  for each road above, each with a control beside it showing the honest
  request still works. Most were also run with their fix taken out, and
  failed; the scenario notes which, beside each check.
- Daggerheart 2.10.5's own code runs in the headless harness, copied
  unchanged, so the Daggerheart checks are measured against the real thing.
- An independent review of the stage found ordinary Daggerheart play reported
  to the GM as tampering, a Fear limit that refused a real roll and two
  rerolls, a Truth Bullet record that never ran at load, and a few gaps in
  what a Reroll may take back. All are fixed here and have checks.
- Not checked in a real Foundry yet, and listed in the audit's live checks:
  that Foundry names the sender of a Daggerheart request, the socket functions
  the guard needs, whether the ownership window's save fires the update hook,
  the order a Reroll's two messages reach the GM, how a long drag is split,
  whether on-screen notices escape markup, and how the sheet lock looks.
